sugPrompts: What is a need vs a want?
How much should I save from an allowance?

knowledgeBase.response: Needs are mandatory for your health, safety, and continuing your studies (rent, groceries, transit, course textbooks). Wants are lifestyle extras (dining out, streaming bundles, trendy sneakers). A good target is keeping Wants under 30% of your allowance!
A Need is an essential requirement for survival and education—things like hostel rent, basic food groceries, utility bills, commuter bus passes, and prescribed study materials.
A Want is discretionary spending that makes college fun but isn't strictly mandatory—like specialty coffees, takeout food delivery, video game passes, and new clothes when you already have enough.

The 50/30/20 framework splits your monthly income into:
• 50% for Needs (rent, bills, groceries)
• 30% for Wants (fun, dining, hobbies)
• 20% for Savings (emergency cushion & debt payoff)
If living costs are high, try 60/25/15 instead!

The #1 rule for students: 'Pay Yourself First'! When your allowance or stipend arrives on Day 1, move 15–20% immediately into a separate savings pot before you start spending. Don't rely on saving whatever loose change remains at month-end!
Try the 24-Hour Rule! When you see an item online or in a shop, wait a full day before tapping checkout. 70% of the time, the emotional urge passes and you keep that cash in your wallet.
Aim to build a starter $200–$300 emergency buffer in college. It protects you from panic whenever a phone display cracks, unexpected dental filling is needed, or a textbook fee arises.

Audit recurring charges monthly! Always use your student (.edu) email for student discounts, rotate streaming platforms one at a time, and set calendar alerts to cancel free trials before they auto-renew.
